images.title: Angle bisector by folding
images.purpose: Show that a crease which halves an angle is an angle bisector.
images.composition: One right angle centred with plenty of empty space around it.
images.exact_structure: One right angle of 90° with two teal #0072B2 arms from a vertex and a small square corner mark. One dashed reddish purple #CC79A7 crease from the vertex exactly halfway between the arms, making 2 equal angles of 45°. Exactly 2 arms, 1 crease, 2 equal angles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a crease that does not split the angle into two equal parts
images.takeaway: An angle bisector halves an angle.
images.description: A right angle of 90° with a dashed crease through the middle splitting it into two equal 45° angles, the crease labelled bisector.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the crease and say why the two small angles are equal.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture of the angle itself; one clean image carries it.
